goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:24 — host values string-interpolated into raw SQL (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)); quotes break the migration; should use quote or parameterized insert

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops through `records.each do |h|` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` table value (the old `embeddable_hosts` setting), and builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any stored host line contains a single quote or other SQL-significant characters, the SQL will break (at minimum) and could potentially be exploited in a compromised DB scenario. Rails migrations should use `quote(h)` / `connection.quote(h)` or insert via AR to avoid this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201 — for any *_ids key the original attribute is unconditionally deleted and replaced with lookups even when _lookupSubType returns undefined for every id, losing plain foo_ids data with no side-loaded collection

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In store.js.es6, the regex was expanded from /(.+)\_id$/ to /(.+)\_id(s?)$/ so keys ending in *_ids now match. For the plural case (m[2] truthy), the code maps ids through _lookupSubType and then unconditionally does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k];`. Since `map` always returns an array (even if every lookup returns undefined), this always deletes the original `foo_ids` attribute, losing the raw ids when there is no matching sideloaded collection to hydrate from (a behavior change from before, where *_ids was left untouched).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197 — obj[k].map(...) throws TypeError when a *_ids value is null; the `hydrated || []` guard is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In the updated `_hydrateEmbedded`, when a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` and the optional `s` is present (i.e. `*_ids`), the code unconditionally executes `obj[k].map(...)`. If `obj[k]` is `null` (or any non-array), this will throw a `TypeError` before `hydrated || []` can apply, making that fallback ineffective for nulls. There is no guard like `Array.isArray(obj[k])` or `obj[k] || []` before calling `map`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,7 — format regex accepts a :port suffix but record_for_host compares against uri.host without port, so hosts saved as example.com:8080 can never match

adjudication.rationale: Yes. EmbeddableHost validates `host` with a regex that allows an optional `:port` suffix (e.g. `example.com:8080`). The `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so such a value can be persisted as `example.com:8080`. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. `uri.host` excludes the port, so it will be `example.com`, which will never match a stored `example.com:8080`, making port-specific saved hosts effectively unusable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — resources :embeddable_hosts exposes index, show, new, edit which don't exist on the controller; restrict with only: [:create, :update, :destroy]

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the diff adds `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new`, which by default creates routes for index/show/new/edit (GET) in addition to create/update/destroy. But the new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` in the diff only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy`. Hitting the generated GET routes (e.g., `/admin/embeddable_hosts`, `/admin/embeddable_hosts/:id`) would raise `AbstractController::ActionNotFound` since those actions don't exist. Restricting the routes with `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` would avoid exposing broken endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-') replaces only the first underscore, so multi-word admin model names fail the ADMIN_MODELS lookup; use a global regex

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ADMIN_MODELS` contains only `plugin`, `site-customization`, and `embeddable-host`. The corresponding Ember Data types that would be passed to `basePath` would be `plugin`, `site_customization`, and `embeddable_host`, each containing at most one underscore. Therefore `type.replace('_', '-')` is sufficient for all admin models introduced/used here, and the “multi-word admin model names” concern is hypothetical (not verifiable from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 and admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — PUT /admin/customize/embedding and the saveChanges action do nothing but re-render and are unreachable from the template; dead endpoint/action

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders the current OpenStruct-based embedding object and does not persist anything. On the client, admin-embedding.js.es6 defines a saveChanges action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would hit PUT /admin/customize/embedding via the new embedding adapter path. However, the new template `embedding.hbs` never triggers `saveChanges` (it only renders per-host save/delete via the embeddable-host component and an `addHost` button). So both the PUT endpoint and the controller action are effectively unused from the UI, and even if invoked they perform no update.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb contain only subclass assertions; no coverage of create/update/destroy, the uncategorized fallback, nil-host handling, or the migration's data conversion

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`. Each contains only a single example asserting the controller class inherits from `Admin::AdminController`, and does not exercise any controller actions. In particular, there are no tests for `create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, no test of the uncategorized fallback in `save_host`, and no tests around behavior when the record lookup returns nil. There is also no spec covering the migration’s conversion of old `site_settings` values into `embeddable_hosts` rows. This is a verifiable lack of meaningful test coverage introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 — no test for a *_ids attribute with no matching side-loaded collection or a null *_ids value

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` to hydrate `*_ids` arrays, but it does not touch or show any `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` file. From the diff alone, you cannot verify what tests exist or don’t exist in that file, so the claim "no test for a *_ids attribute with no matching side-loaded collection or a null *_ids value" is not directly verifiable. (There may be an edge-case risk in the new code if `obj[k]` is null, but the proposed finding is specifically about missing tests in a file not shown/modified here.)
